title: The Road to Reims
description: June-July 1429. After the victory at Orleans, Joan of Arc must escort the Dauphin Charles through English-held territory to the cathedral at Reims for his coronation. English garrisons at Troyes and Chalons block the route and can be fought or persuaded to surrender. Victory requires the Dauphin reaching Reims cathedral alive; his death means defeat.

anachronisms_found: The English garrison force is built around 9 CROSSBOWMEN with no LONGBOWMAN, even though the editor offers the Longbowman — the signature English missile arm of the 1420s is simply absent, and crossbows read as continental/Burgundian rather than English.
Narration calls Charles the 'boy-king'; the Dauphin was 26 in July 1429 and had been a functioning claimant for years — a factual mislabel, not an engine limit.

Troyes and Châlons are labelled purely 'England's' with an 'English Garrison Commander'; both towns were held by Anglo-BURGUNDIAN garrisons under Burgundian civic authority, and no Burgundian player or unit appears anywhere in the roster.
